raw_record.question_text:
In the transition-state structure shown in the image, calculate the total number of bonds in the structure, including single, double, and triple bonds but excluding those involving hydrogen.

Note: Disregard arrows. Consider all components present in the transition-state structure shown in the image.

method.method_draft: Inspect the transition-state drawing and divide it into visible components. Count the heavy-atom bonds in the left bicyclic carbon framework as 8, counting the displayed C=C as one bond. Count the single bond from that framework to the amine nitrogen as 1. Count the five edges of the pyrrolidine ring attached to that nitrogen as 5. Count the six perimeter bonds of the right-hand six-membered heterocycle as 6, counting each double bond as one bond. Add all components while disregarding arrows: 8 + 1 + 5 + 6 = 20.

method.method_draft: Convert the drawing into a heavy-atom graph after ignoring arrows and hydrogens. Count heavy atoms: 7 in the left bicyclic carbon skeleton, 5 in the attached pyrrolidine ring including N, and 6 in the right heterocycle, giving V = 18. Count connected components: the left amine/bicyclic/pyrrolidine structure is one component and the right heterocycle is another, so C = 2. Count independent cycles: the bicyclic framework contributes 2, the pyrrolidine ring contributes 1, and the right heterocycle contributes 1, so R = 4. Apply E = V - C + R = 18 - 2 + 4 = 20 heavy-atom bonds.
